proposal.summary: CSRF in Jenkins Frugal Testing Plugin <= 1.1 allows attackers to perform actions using attacker-specified credentials and retrieve test IDs/names from Frugal Testing when a valid credential corresponds to the attacker-specified username.
proposal.affected_product: Jenkins Frugal Testing Plugin 1.1 and earlier
proposal.cwe_quote: A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Jenkins Frugal Testing Plugin 1.1 and earlier allows attackers to connect to Frugal Testing using attacker-specified credentials, and to retrieve test IDs and names from Frugal Testing, if a valid credential corresponds to the attacker-specified username.

AV.quote: A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Jenkins Frugal Testing Plugin 1.1 and earlier allows attackers to connect to Frugal Testing using attacker-specified credentials, and to retrieve test IDs and names from Frugal Testing, if a valid credential corresponds to the attacker-specified username.

C.quote: allows attackers to ... retrieve test IDs and names from Frugal Testing

I.quote: allows attackers to ... retrieve test IDs and names from Frugal Testing

A.quote: allows attackers to connect to Frugal Testing using attacker-specified credentials

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify the vulnerability by reproducing the CSRF request against a test Jenkins instance with the plugin installed, and if confirmed, update the plugin to a patched version or implement CSRF protections (require valid anti-CSRF tokens) and rotate any impacted credentials.
